C0.quote: choose one alternative as the winner using a mechanism
C0.note: Distributed voting rules (districts) and their distortion; strategyproofness also studied.

C1.quote: we also experimentally compare the distortion of many different mechanisms
C1.note: Main results are distortion bounds (WD). Strategyproof mechanism results are SB. Experiments use synthetic and real data (Jester). AX is a weak fit, since the lower bounds concern all mechanisms rather than properties, so it is not included in the primary.

C2.1.value: preferences of the agents; valuation profile; ordinal profile
C2.1.quote: valuation profile consisting of the valuation functions of all agents

C2.2.quote: exact cardinal information about the valuation functions, or only ordinal information
C2.2.note: Cardinal mechanisms take valuations; ordinal mechanisms take rankings.

C2.3.quote: The preferences of each agent 𝑖 ∈ 𝑁 are captured by a valuation function

C2.4.quote: it may be able to use exact cardinal information about the valuation functions
C2.4.note: Mechanisms are applied directly to valuations or consistent rankings. Rankings are defined as induced by values. Outside strategyproofness, there is no statement about submission or reporting.

C3.1.quote: providing false information never leads to the selection of an alternative
C3.1.note: Strategyproofness analyses consider misreports; distortion analyses do not.

C3.2.note: The distortion analyses do not state that voters submit their held attitude.

C4.1.note: Ordinal inputs are defined as consistent with the values (σ_i(a)<σ_i(b) if v_i(a)≥v_i(b)), so the link is specified. However, the applicability condition is met because RANK is included and welfare and distortion are used. Code SPEC.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.loc: Section 2, Social Welfare and Distortion, p.1393
C5.1.quote: The efficiency of a distributed mechanism is measured by the notion of distortion.
C5.1.note: Distortion and social welfare are the central criteria.

C5.2.quote: the social welfare of an alternative 𝑎 ∈ 𝐴 is the total value
C5.2.note: Welfare is evaluated on the cardinal valuations, which are separate from the ordinal input.

VOT.note: Voters are strategic only in the strategyproofness analyses and are otherwise fixed as inputs. Information is not specified, although dominant strategy is the implied concept.
